assetQuality.title: NPL ratio and allowance coverage
assetQuality.content:
The non-performing loan (NPL) ratio is loans more than 90 days overdue (or otherwise impaired) as a percentage of gross loans. Allowance coverage is loan-loss reserves held against NPLs -- above 100% means reserves exceed the stock of bad loans.

For China CITIC Bank: the NPL ratio has fallen every year since FY2019 (1.65% to 1.15% FY2025) while coverage rose from 175% to over 200%, i.e. both the problem shrank and the cushion against it grew -- a genuine improvement, not reserve releases propping up earnings.

What to watch:

  • Coverage falling while the NPL ratio is flat or rising (reserve release into earnings)
  • NPL ratio ticking up during a credit cycle turn, especially in property-developer exposure

creditCostRoaa.title: Credit cost and ROAA
creditCostRoaa.content:
Credit cost is the annualized loan-impairment charge divided by average loans -- the through-the-cycle cost of lending. ROAA (return on average assets) is net income divided by average total assets, the standard cross-bank profitability measure since it is not distorted by leverage differences the way ROE is.

For China CITIC Bank: credit cost has roughly halved from 1.79% (FY2019) to 0.89% (FY2025) as asset quality improved, but ROAA has stayed flat-to-down (0.76% to 0.73%) over the same period -- the credit-cost tailwind has been absorbed by NIM compression, not passed through to higher returns.

What to watch:

  • Credit cost re-accelerating faster than ROAA can absorb
  • ROAA versus large Chinese state banks, typically 0.7-1.0%

feeIncome.title: Net fee and commission income
feeIncome.content:
Net fee and commission income is non-interest revenue -- wealth management, cards, settlement and agency fees -- net of fee expense. Plotted in log scale against total revenue (net interest income + fees + other) to show the mix shift.

For China CITIC Bank: fee income has been roughly flat to down since FY2019 (RMB46bn to RMB33bn FY2025) even as total revenue grew, so the bank has become more, not less, dependent on net interest income -- the opposite of the fee-diversification story many banks target to offset NIM compression.

What to watch:

  • Fee income share of revenue rising (diversification) versus falling (NIM dependence deepening)
  • Wealth-management AUM growth, which drives this line at Chinese banks

ordinaryEquity.title: Ordinary shareholders' equity vs total equity
ordinaryEquity.content:
Ordinary shareholders' equity is total equity less preference shares and perpetual bonds -- the capital that actually belongs to A/H ordinary shareholders and backs the per-share book value. Total equity (the ShareholdersEquity column elsewhere on this page) includes those instruments.

For China CITIC Bank: the gap was over RMB100bn by FY2025 (RMB828.8bn total vs RMB723.9bn ordinary) -- preference shares and perpetual bonds carry fixed coupons paid ahead of ordinary dividends and only convert to equity on a 5.125% CET1 trigger, so BookValuePerShare and the DCF are built on the ordinary figure, not the larger total.

What to watch:

  • The gap widening (more hybrid capital issuance) versus ordinary equity compounding faster (retained-earnings growth)
  • Any approach toward the CET1 conversion trigger on the preference shares

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
